p.src: Now, when Lady Wang saw that the Lady Dowager had merely caught a slight chill in the Prospect Garden that day and was not seriously ill, and that she had recovered after the doctor prescribed two doses of medicine, she set her mind at ease. She then summoned Xifeng and instructed her to prepare the things that were to be sent to Jia Zheng. While they were discussing the arrangements, a servant arrived with a summons from the Lady Dowager, and Lady Wang promptly took Xifeng with her to see her. Lady Wang asked again, “Are you feeling much better now?” “I am much better today,” replied the Lady Dowager. “A little while ago I tasted the young pheasant soup you sent. It was quite savory, and I ate two pieces of the meat as well. It did me a world of good.” Lady Wang smiled. “That was a token of Xifeng’s devotion to you, Old Ancestress. Her devotion has proved sincere; all the affection you ordinarily lavish on her has not been wasted.” The Lady Dowager nodded with a smile. “It was thoughtful of her to remember me. If any uncooked meat remains, have another couple of pieces fried and salted well. They would give some flavor to my congee. Good as the soup is, it does not go well with congee.” Xifeng promptly assented and sent someone to carry the instructions to the kitchen.

p.src: The Lady Dowager then turned to Lady Wang and said with a smile, “I sent for you on no other account than this. The second is Xifeng’s birthday. For the past two years I had meant well in advance to celebrate it for her, but whenever the day drew near some important affair arose, and it was allowed to pass unnoticed. This year everyone is here, and nothing seems likely to intervene, so let us all enjoy ourselves properly for a day.” Lady Wang smiled. “I have been thinking the same thing. Since it pleases you, Old Ancestress, why should we not settle the arrangements now?” The Lady Dowager said with a smile, “In past years, no matter whose birthday it was, everyone presented a separate gift. That has grown rather commonplace, and it makes us seem like strangers to one another. Today I have devised a new plan that will neither seem distant nor lack amusement.” Lady Wang hastened to reply, “Whatever plan you think best, Old Ancestress, is the one we shall follow.” The Lady Dowager smiled. “I thought we might imitate humbler households and all subscribe to a common fund, then arrange the celebration according to however much money we collect. Would that not be fun?” “That is an excellent idea,” said Lady Wang with a smile, “but how are the shares to be apportioned?” This response delighted the Lady Dowager all the more. She promptly sent servants to invite Aunt Xue, Lady Xing, and the others, and also summoned the young ladies and Baoyu. From the other mansion she called for Zhen’s wife, as well as the wife of Lai Da and the other senior, respected stewardesses.

p.src: Seeing the Lady Dowager in such high spirits, all the maids and matrons were delighted too. They hurried off in different directions, some to invite the guests and others to pass on the summons. In less time than it took to eat a meal, old and young, mistresses and servants, had crowded the room into a dark, dense throng. Only Aunt Xue sat facing the Lady Dowager. Lady Xing and Lady Wang occupied two chairs by the chamber door; Baochai and five or six of the other young ladies sat on the kang; Baoyu sat nestled before the Lady Dowager; and the floor was packed with people standing shoulder to shoulder. The Lady Dowager quickly ordered several low stools to be brought for Lai Da’s mother and the other elderly, respected matrons. It was the custom in the Jia household that aged servants who had attended the older generation were shown even greater respect than the younger masters. Thus You-shi, Xifeng, and the others remained standing on the floor, while Lai Da’s mother and three or four other old matrons apologized for the liberty before seating themselves on the low stools.

p.src: With a smile, the Lady Dowager repeated to everyone what she had just proposed. Who among them would not gladly join in such amusement? Some were fond of Xifeng, some willingly favored the scheme, while others feared her and were only too eager to curry favor with her. Besides, they could all afford the expense. So as soon as they heard the proposal, they gladly agreed. The Lady Dowager began. “I shall contribute twenty taels.” Aunt Xue smiled. “I shall follow your lead, Old Ancestress, and contribute twenty taels as well.” Lady Xing and Lady Wang said, “We would not presume to rank ourselves beside you, Old Ancestress. Naturally we must stand one degree lower, so we shall contribute sixteen taels each.” You-shi and Li Wan also smiled. “Then naturally we must stand another degree lower and contribute twelve taels each.” The Lady Dowager hastily said to Li Wan, “You are a widow without an income. How could we make you contribute this money? I shall pay your share for you.” Xifeng quickly interposed with a smile, “Do not get carried away yet, Old Ancestress. First reckon up the account before taking on another obligation. You already have two shares to pay, and now you want to contribute another twelve taels for my elder sister-in-law. You may say so cheerfully now, but in a little while, when you think it over, your heart will ache. Afterward you will say, ‘All that money was spent on Xifeng,’ and devise some clever scheme to coax three or four more shares out of me in secret to make up your loss. I will not be taken in!” Her words made everyone laugh. The Lady Dowager laughed. “Then what do you propose?” Xifeng replied with a smile, “My birthday has not even arrived, yet already I have been so overwhelmed by this honor that I can scarcely bear it. I am not being allowed to contribute a single cash myself, and I am truly uneasy at troubling so many people. I had better pay my elder sister-in-law’s share for her. On the day itself I shall eat a little more, and that will be blessing enough for me.” Lady Xing and the others all agreed that this was most reasonable. Only then did the Lady Dowager consent. Xifeng smiled again. “There is one more thing I should like to say. As I see it, the Old Ancestress is contributing twenty taels for herself, besides paying the two shares for Cousin Lin and Brother Bao. Aunt Xue is contributing twenty taels for herself and one share for Sister Bao. That is fair enough. But the two ladies are each contributing only sixteen taels, less than either of you, and are paying no one else’s share. That is somewhat unfair. The Old Ancestress is being made to suffer a loss!” The Lady Dowager hastened to say with a laugh, “My Xifeng is the only one who takes my side. What you say is perfectly right. If not for you, they would have taken me in yet again.” Xifeng smiled. “Old Ancestress, simply assign those two girls to the two ladies, one apiece. However large or small their allotted contributions may be, each lady need only pay one share for one of them.” The Lady Dowager promptly declared, “That is perfectly fair. We shall do just so.” Lai Da’s mother hurriedly rose and said with a laugh, “This turns everything upside down! I must speak up for the two ladies.”

p.src: Over there you are her daughter-in-law, and here you are her own niece; yet instead of siding with your mother-in-law and cousin, you side with someone else. This daughter-in-law has become a complete stranger, and her own niece has actually turned into an outsider!” Her words sent Grandmother Jia and everyone else into peals of laughter. Lai Da’s mother then asked, “Since the young mistresses are giving twelve taels, naturally we ought to give one grade less.” Hearing this, Grandmother Jia said, “That will not do. Your rank may be a grade lower, but I know that you few are all wealthy women; though your standing is lower, you have more money than they do. You must contribute on the same scale as they do.” The matrons promptly agreed. Grandmother Jia continued, “The young ladies need only make a token contribution—one month’s allowance apiece will do.” Then she turned and called for Yuanyang. “You girls should gather a few people too, discuss it among yourselves, and pool your contributions.” Yuanyang assented and soon returned with Ping’er, Xiren, Caixia, several other young maids, and their contributions, some of two taels and some of one. Grandmother Jia asked Ping’er, “Surely you are giving your mistress a birthday present yourself? Why are you joining this collection too?” Ping’er smiled. “I have made a separate private contribution. This one is for the common fund, so I ought to pay my share here too.” Grandmother Jia smiled. “That is a good girl.” Xifeng laughed again. “Now everyone above and below has been included. But there are still the two secondary wives. We should ask whether they wish to contribute too. It is only right to extend the courtesy to them; otherwise they may think we look down on them.” Grandmother Jia hastily replied, “Of course! How could we have forgotten them? They may not be free, though. Send a maid to ask them.” Even as she spoke, a maid went off and returned some time later to report, “They will each give two taels.” Grandmother Jia said delightedly, “Bring brush and inkstone and calculate the exact total.” You-shi quietly scolded Xifeng, “You insatiable little minx! All these mothers and aunts are pooling silver to celebrate your birthday, yet that still is not enough for you, and you drag those two poor creatures into it as well. What for?” Xifeng also laughed softly. “Stop talking nonsense. Once we leave here, I shall settle accounts with you. Why should those two be considered unfortunate? Any money they have merely goes to support others; better to make them contribute so that we can enjoy ourselves.”

p.src: While they were speaking, the reckoning was completed: they had collected more than one hundred and fifty taels in all. Grandmother Jia said, “A single day of opera and feasting could never use all that.” You-shi said, “Since no guests are being invited and there will not be many banquet tables, it would cover the expenses of two or three days. Above all, the opera costs us nothing, so we save on that.” Grandmother Jia said, “Send for whichever troupe Xifeng says is good.” Xifeng said, “We have heard our household troupe so often that we know it by heart. We might as well spend a little and bring in another troupe for a change.” Grandmother Jia said, “I shall leave this matter to Cousin Zhen’s wife. Let Xifeng concern herself with nothing at all, so that she may truly enjoy herself for one day.” You-shi agreed. After they had talked a while longer, everyone saw that Grandmother Jia was tired, and they gradually took their leave.

p.src: After You-shi and the others had seen Lady Xing and Lady Wang off, they went to Xifeng’s room to discuss the arrangements for the birthday celebration. Xifeng said, “There is no need to ask me. Just watch the old lady’s expression and act accordingly.” You-shi laughed. “You little creature, you really have had an extraordinary stroke of luck! I wondered what business we had been summoned for, but it turns out to have been solely about this. Not only must I contribute money, I must also take charge of everything. How will you thank me?” Xifeng laughed. “Stop being silly! I did not ask you to come, so why should I thank you? Are you afraid of the trouble? Then go and tell the old lady right now, and she can appoint someone else.” You-shi laughed. “Just look how carried away she is! I advise you to restrain yourself a little. Fill a vessel too full and it spills over.” The two talked a while longer before parting.

p.src: The next day the silver was delivered to the Ningguo mansion. You-shi had only just risen and was dressing when she asked who had brought it. The maids replied, “Mistress Lin.” You-shi ordered them to bring her in. A maid went to the servants’ quarters and summoned Lin Zhixiao’s wife. You-shi had her sit on the footstool and, as she busied herself dressing, asked, “How much silver is there in this packet?” Lin Zhixiao’s wife replied, “This is the silver contributed by those of us below. We pooled ours and sent it over first. The old lady’s and the ladies’ contributions have not arrived yet.” As they spoke, the maids announced, “The ladies and secondary wives from the other mansion have sent someone with their contributions.” You-shi laughingly scolded them. “You little wretches remember nothing but such trivial expressions! Yesterday the old lady was merely in high spirits and deliberately imitated humble families by proposing a collection. Yet you remembered the expression, and now you speak of it as though it were something solemn and official. Hurry and receive it, serve the messengers tea properly, and then see them off.” The maids assented and hurriedly brought the contributions in. There were two packets in all, including Baochai’s and Daiyu’s shares. You-shi asked whose contributions were still missing. Lin Zhixiao’s wife replied, “We still lack those of the old lady, the ladies, the young mistresses, and the junior maids.” You-shi asked, “What about your senior mistress’s contribution?” Lin Zhixiao’s wife replied, “When you go over there, madam, you will find that all the silver is being disbursed through the second mistress; every share is included.”

p.src: As they spoke, Lady You finished washing and dressing, ordered a carriage prepared, and presently arrived at the Rong mansion, where she first went to see Xifeng. She found that Xifeng had already wrapped up the silver and was just about to send it over. Lady You asked, “Is it all here?” Xifeng laughed. “It is all there. Hurry and take it away. If you lose it, I won’t be responsible.” Lady You laughed. “I don’t entirely trust you. I had better count it here in front of you.” She thereupon counted the shares one by one, and sure enough, Li Wan’s contribution alone was missing. Lady You laughed. “I knew you were up to some devilry! Why isn’t your elder sister-in-law’s share here?” Xifeng laughed. “Isn’t all that enough to spend? One share less won’t matter. If it proves insufficient, I’ll give you more.” Lady You said, “Yesterday you played the generous lady in front of everyone, and today you are trying to wriggle out of it with me. I absolutely won’t allow that. I shall go straight to the Old Lady and ask her for it.” Xifeng laughed. “I see you are formidable. The next time something comes up, I too shall insist that every nail be matched to its proper hole, and you mustn’t complain.” Lady You laughed. “So there are things even you fear. If you had not always treated me so dutifully, I certainly would not let you off.” As she spoke, she took out Ping’er’s contribution and called, “Ping’er, come here! Take your share back. If the money runs short, I shall make it up for you.” Ping’er understood her meaning and said, “Please use it for now, madam. If anything is left over, you may reward me with it afterward.” Lady You laughed. “So your mistress may bend the rules, but I may not show you a little favor?” Ping’er had no choice but to take it back. Lady You added, “Your mistress is so calculating—what does she mean to do with all this money she scrapes together? If she cannot spend it all, perhaps she means to take it into her coffin and spend it there.” Still talking, she made her way to Grandmother Jia’s quarters. After paying her respects and exchanging a few general remarks, she went to Yuanyang’s room to consult with her, intending to follow Yuanyang’s advice on how best to please Grandmother Jia. The two of them settled all the arrangements. Before leaving, Lady You also returned Yuanyang’s two taels of silver, saying, “There is more than enough without this.” With that, she came away and went to spend a while talking with Lady Wang. When Lady Wang entered the Buddhist chapel, Lady You returned Caiyun’s contribution to her as well. Seeing that Xifeng was not present, she then returned the contributions of Zhou and Zhao as well. The two women did not dare accept them. Lady You said, “You poor things, where would you find spare money like this? Even if that girl Feng finds out, I shall answer for it.” On hearing this, the two thanked her over and over before finally accepting the money. Lady You then came straight out, boarded her carriage, and returned home. There is no more to be said of this.

u.src: After paying her respects and exchanging a few general remarks, she went to Yuanyang’s room to consult with her, intending to follow Yuanyang’s advice on how best to please Grandmother Jia.
The two of them settled all the arrangements.
Before leaving, Lady You also returned Yuanyang’s two taels of silver, saying, “There is more than enough without this.”
With that, she came away and went to spend a while talking with Lady Wang.
When Lady Wang entered the Buddhist chapel, Lady You returned Caiyun’s contribution to her as well.
Seeing that Xifeng was not present, she then returned the contributions of Zhou and Zhao as well.
The two women did not dare accept them.
Lady You said, “You poor things, where would you find spare money like this?
Even if that girl Feng finds out, I shall answer for it.”
On hearing this, the two thanked her over and over before finally accepting the money.
Lady You then came straight out, boarded her carriage, and returned home.
There is no more to be said of this.

p.src: In the blink of an eye, the second day of the ninth month arrived. Everyone in the Garden had learned that Lady You was preparing a splendid celebration: there would be not only opera but acrobats and both male and female storytellers, and they all looked forward to a day of merriment. Li Wan reminded the other young ladies, “Today is the proper day for our poetry club, so do not forget it. Baoyu has not come either. I suppose he cares only for the excitement and has cast refinement aside.” She then ordered a maid to see what he was doing and ask him to come at once. The maid was gone for quite some time before returning to report, “Elder Sister Hua says he went out early this morning.” They were all astonished. “There is no possible reason for him to have gone out. That foolish girl does not know what she is talking about.” They therefore sent Cuimo to inquire again. Presently Cuimo returned and said, “He really has gone out. They say a friend of his died and he has gone to pay his respects.” Tanchun said, “That cannot possibly be true. Whatever may have happened, there is no reason for him to go out today. Ask Xiren to come here. I shall question her.” She had barely finished speaking when Xiren appeared. Li Wan and the others all said, “Whatever business he may have today, he still should not have gone out. First, it is your Second Mistress’s birthday, and the Old Lady is so delighted that everyone in both mansions is coming to join the festivities, yet he has gone away. Second, it is the appointed day of our first poetry-club meeting, and he has left without even asking permission!” Xiren sighed. “He told me last night that he had urgent business at Prince Beijing’s mansion early this morning and would hurry back. I urged him not to go, but he refused to listen. Then this morning he asked for mourning clothes. Perhaps some important concubine in Prince Beijing’s household has died, though I cannot be sure.” Li Wan and the others said, “If that is truly the case, he was right to pay a visit, but he should be back by now.” They then agreed among themselves, “Let us go on composing poems. When he comes back, we shall punish him.” They had barely finished speaking when a servant arrived with a summons from Grandmother Jia, so they all went to the front apartments. When Xiren reported Baoyu’s absence, Grandmother Jia was displeased and ordered someone to fetch him.

p.src: In fact, Baoyu had a private matter on his mind. The day before, he had instructed Mingyan, “I am going out early tomorrow morning. Have two horses ready at the rear gate, and do not let anyone else follow me. Tell Li Gui that I have gone to the northern mansion. If anyone comes looking for me, have him stop them from searching and merely say that they have kept me there, but that I shall be back before long.” Mingyan could make neither head nor tail of this, but he had no choice but to pass on the instructions. Sure enough, early that morning two horses were waiting at the rear gate of the Garden. At daybreak Baoyu emerged from the side gate dressed entirely in plain white. Without uttering a word, he mounted, bent low over the saddle, and galloped away down the street. Mingyan had no choice but to leap onto the other horse, urge it after him, and call anxiously from behind, “Where are we going?” Baoyu asked, “Where does this road lead?” Mingyan replied, “This is the main road to the north gate. Beyond it, the country is deserted and there is nowhere to amuse oneself.” Baoyu nodded. “A deserted place is exactly what I want.” With that, he plied his whip all the harder, and before long his horse had rounded two bends and passed through the city gate. Mingyan was more bewildered than ever and could only follow close behind.

p.src: After galloping seven or eight li without pause, they reached a place where the signs of habitation gradually thinned. Only then did Baoyu rein in his horse and turn to ask Mingyan, “Is there anywhere here that sells incense?” “There is incense to be had,” said Mingyan, “but what kind do you want?” Baoyu considered. “Other incense will not do. It must be sandalwood, rue, and aloeswood.” Mingyan laughed. “Those three will be hard to find.” Baoyu was at a loss. Seeing his difficulty, Mingyan asked, “What do you need the incense for? I often see loose incense in the little sachets you carry, Second Master. Why not look through them?” The suggestion reminded Baoyu. Reaching back, he pulled a sachet from the front of his robe and felt inside. To his delight, it contained two tiny pieces of fine aloeswood. “It is only rather disrespectful to use these.” But then he reflected that incense he had carried on his own person was in fact better than any he might buy. He then asked about a censer and charcoal. “You may as well give up on that,” said Mingyan. Where could we find them out in this wilderness? If you needed all these things, why did you not say so earlier? We could have brought them with us and saved ourselves the trouble.” “You muddlehead!” said Baoyu. “If I could have brought them, would I have ridden off like this as though fleeing for my life?” Mingyan thought for quite a while, then smiled. “I have an idea, though I do not know whether it will please you, Second Master. I imagine you will need more than these things and may want something else as well. That need not pose a problem. Another two li along the road ahead will bring us to the Water Immortal Convent.” Baoyu hurriedly asked, “Is the Water Immortal Convent near here? So much the better! Let us go there.” With that he urged his horse forward, turning as he rode to say to Mingyan, “The nun from the Water Immortal Convent often visits our house. If we go there and ask to borrow a censer, she will certainly agree.” Mingyan said, “Quite apart from the fact that her convent enjoys your family’s patronage, even at a temple that had no connection with us at all, they would not dare refuse if we asked to borrow one. But there is one thing: I have always seen how much you detest the Water Immortal Convent. Why are you so pleased with it today?” Baoyu replied, “What I have always hated is the way vulgar people, without understanding the reason for anything, worship gods indiscriminately and build temples at random. In former times, rich old men and foolish wealthy women would hear of some deity and erect a temple to worship it, without even knowing who the deity was. They heard a few unofficial histories and romances and took them for truth. Take this Water Immortal Convent: because the Goddess of the Luo is enshrined inside, it is called the Water Immortal Convent. Yet in truth there was never any Goddess of the Luo in ancient times. She was merely a fiction of Cao Zijian’s, but these fools made an image of her and set it up for worship. Today, however, the place happens to suit what is in my heart, so I shall make use of it.”

p.src: As they spoke, they had already reached the gate. The elderly nun was utterly astonished to see Baoyu arrive—as though a living dragon had dropped from heaven. She hurried forward to greet him and ordered an old Taoist attendant to take his horse. Baoyu went inside. He did not bow to the image of the Goddess of the Luo, but merely studied it with admiration. Though fashioned from clay, it truly possessed the bearing of one “light as a startled swan, graceful as a wandering dragon,” and the beauty of “a lotus rising from green waves, the morning sun aglow in rosy clouds.” Before he knew it, tears fell from Baoyu’s eyes. The old nun served him tea. Baoyu then asked her to lend him a censer. The nun was gone for some time and returned having prepared not only a censer, but incense, offerings, and paper horses as well. “I need none of those things,” said Baoyu. He ordered Mingyan to carry the censer into the rear courtyard and choose a clean spot, but they could not find one anywhere. “How about the platform around the well?” Mingyan suggested. Baoyu nodded. Together they went to the well platform and set down the censer.

“I need none of those things,” said Baoyu.

p.src: Mingyan stood to one side. Baoyu took out the incense and lit it. With tears in his eyes, he made a half-bow, then turned and ordered Mingyan to put everything away. Mingyan answered, but instead of putting it away, he hastily dropped to his knees, knocked his head several times, and prayed aloud: “I, Mingyan, have served Second Master for several years, and there is no thought of his that I do not know. Only today’s offering was not disclosed to me, and I dare not ask about it. Though I know neither the name nor the family of the departed spirit receiving this offering, she must surely have been a young lady unique in the human world and without equal in heaven, supremely intelligent and supremely elegant. Second Master cannot speak what is in his heart, so let me pray on his behalf: if your fragrant spirit is aware and your gentle soul still cherishes affection, then although the realms of yin and yang divide you, since you are kindred spirits, there can be no harm in coming often to visit Second Master. From the netherworld, pray protect Second Master, so that in his next life he too may become a girl and keep you company, and never again be reborn as one of these foul, bearded creatures!” When he had finished, he knocked his head several more times before rising.

p.src: Before Mingyan had even finished, Baoyu could no longer suppress his laughter. He kicked him and said, “Stop talking nonsense! If anyone hears you, they will laugh at us.” Mingyan rose, put away the censer, and walked with Baoyu, saying, “I have already told the nun that you have not eaten, Second Master, and asked her to prepare whatever she has so that you might force yourself to eat a little. I know there is a grand banquet at home today and the place is tremendously lively, and that you slipped away for that very reason. In any case, spending a quiet day here will fully discharge your obligation. But you absolutely must not go without food.” Baoyu said, “Since I am taking no part in the theatricals or drinking, there can be no harm in eating a little plain vegetarian food.” “That is just as it should be,” said Mingyan. There is one more thing: now that we have come away, there are still people worrying about us. If no one were worrying, what harm would there be in entering the city late?” But since someone is worrying, you really must return to the city and go home, Second Master. First, the Old Lady and Her Ladyship will be reassured; second, you have already fulfilled your obligation. That is all there is to it. Even if you go home to watch the plays and drink wine, it will not be because you chose to do so, but merely because you are accompanying your parents and fulfilling your filial duty. If, solely on account of this, you disregard the Old Lady and leave Her Ladyship anxious, even the departed spirit to whom you have just made your offering will know no peace. What do you think of what I have said, Second Master?” Baoyu laughed. “I have guessed what you are thinking. Since you alone followed me out here, you are afraid that you will be blamed when we return, so you invoke these grand principles to persuade me. I came only to discharge an obligation. I never said that after doing so I would spend the whole day away from the city instead of returning to drink and watch the plays. Now that I have fulfilled my wish, we can hurry back into the city and set everyone’s mind at rest. Will that not satisfy both duties?” “That is better still,” said Mingyan. As they spoke, the two reached the meditation hall. Sure enough, the nun had laid out a tableful of vegetarian dishes. Baoyu ate a little without much care, and Mingyan ate as well.

p.src: The two mounted their horses and returned by the same road. Mingyan followed behind, repeatedly cautioning him, “Ride carefully, Second Master. This horse is hardly ever ridden, so keep a tight hold on the reins.” Even as he spoke, they entered the city, went in again through the rear gate, and hurried to Happy Red Court. Xiren and the others were all away from the rooms; only a few old serving women remained to watch the place. When they saw him, their faces lit up with joy, and they cried, “Amitabha, you are back at last! Miss Hua has been frantic with worry! They are in the middle of the banquet up there. Hurry along, Second Master.” Hearing this, Baoyu hastily took off his mourning clothes, found festive garments and changed into them, then asked where the banquet was being held. The old women replied that it was in the newly built great flower hall.

p.src: At this, Baoyu went straight to the flower hall, and before he reached it he could already hear the faint strains of singing and instruments. Just as he reached the far side of the passage hall, he saw Yuchuan sitting alone beneath the veranda eaves, shedding tears. The moment she saw him, she checked her tears and said, “The phoenix has arrived! Hurry inside. If you had stayed away any longer, everyone would have rebelled.” Baoyu smiled ingratiatingly and asked, “Can you guess where I went?” Yuchuan did not answer, but merely kept wiping away her tears. Baoyu hurried into the hall and appeared before Grandmother Jia, Lady Wang, and the others, who welcomed him as though they had truly recovered a phoenix. Baoyu promptly stepped forward and paid his respects to Xifeng. Grandmother Jia and Lady Wang both scolded him for having no sense. “How could you run off on your own without saying a word? This is intolerable! If you do this again, once your father comes home, we shall certainly tell him to beat you.” Then they berated the pageboys who had accompanied him for blindly obeying him—going wherever he told them without sending back a single word. At the same time, they questioned him about where exactly he had gone, whether he had eaten anything, and whether he had been frightened. Baoyu merely replied, “One of the Prince of Beijing’s beloved concubines died yesterday, so I went to offer him my condolences. He was weeping so bitterly that I could not very well leave him and come home, so I stayed a little longer.” Grandmother Jia said, “If you ever go out on your own again without telling us first, I shall certainly have your father beat you.” Baoyu promised to obey. When she then proposed having the pageboys beaten, everyone hurried to intercede for them and urged her, “There is no need for Your Ladyship to worry any longer. He is back now, so we should all set our minds at ease and enjoy ourselves for a while.” Grandmother Jia had lashed out only because she had been worried. Now that she saw him safely returned, her joy was more than enough to dispel her anger, and she said no more about it. Instead, fearing that he might feel unwell, that he might not have eaten his fill elsewhere, or that something on the road might have frightened him, she coaxed and comforted him in every possible way. Xiren had already come over to attend him. Everyone resumed watching the play. The play performed that day was The Story of the Thorn Hairpin. Grandmother Jia, Aunt Xue, and the others were so moved that they shed tears; some sighed, while others voiced angry reproaches. To learn what followed, read the next chapter.
